Vysakhan vs State Of Kerala on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35842168/
3  B.A Nos.13725, 13728 and 13730 of 2025  ---------------------------------------
 Dated this the 4th day of December, 2025  ORDER

These applications are filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
2.
The petitioner is common in all the cases.

He is accused No.1 in Crime Nos.1412/2024,
1432/2024 and accused No.2 in Crime No.421/2025 of Vadakkencherry Police Station.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3 read with Section 21, Section 4 read with Section 22 and Section 5 read with Section 23 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Scheme Act.

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Scheme Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case in Crime No.1412/2024 is that accused No. 1 being the Managing Director of the financial institution by name Finspot India Nidhi Ltd. having its branch office at Vadakkencherry received 11,80,000/- from the defacto complainant and Rs.33,00,000/- from his friends as fixed deposits 2025:KER:93936 B.A Nos.13725, 13728 & 13730 of 2025 on believing them that he will give interest with principal, but after receiving the fixed deposit, the accused has not paid the interest and the amount on maturity thereby committed the aforesaid offence.

In Crime no.1432/2024, the accused received Rs.10,00,000/- from the defacto complainant and in Crime no.421/2025 the accused received Rs.13,00,000/- from the defacto complainant, Rs.1,50,000/-
from his wife and Rs.1,00,000/- from his daughter as fixed deposits and failed to pay the interest and the amount on maturity.
4. The petitioner was arrested in these cases on 14.10.2025 and he has been in judicial custody since then.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
6.
Relying on Mohammed Sajjid v. State of Kerala [2025 KHC Online 200], the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that he is entitled to statutory bail.

entities.text: Mohammed Sajjid v. State of Kerala [2025 KHC Online 200]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the police could not complete the investigation and submit the final report.
8. I have gone through the Case Diary.

9. Having regard to the tenure of judicial custody undergone 2025:KER:93936 B.A Nos.13725,
13728 & 13730 of 2025 by the petitioner, I feel that the petitioner is entitled to statutory bail on conditions.

In the result, the Bail Application is allowed as follows:
Vysakhan vs State Of Kerala on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35842168/
4

(a) The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail on his executing bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional court.
(b) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on all Mondays between 10 A.M. and 11 A.M. until further orders.
(c) The petitioner shall not try to influence the prosecution witnesses or attempt to tamper with the evidence.
(d) The petitioner shall surrender his passport before the jurisdictional court.

If he has no passport,
the petitioner shall file an affidavit to that effect.
(e) The petitioner shall not leave State of Kerala without the permission of the jurisdictional court.
2025:KER:93936 B.A Nos.13725, 13728 & 13730 of 2025 (f) The petitioner shall not commit any similar offence while on bail.
(g) If any of the bail conditions are violated by the petitioner, the jurisdictional court will be at liberty to cancel the bail, in accordance with law.

Sd/-
